what: The day-start selectors of shared/dayStart.ts, as a table: which tasks are overdue (lapsed deadline), which slipped (lapsed plan, cascade-aware), which are pinned to today, which are reminded (planned today untimed, due today, counted down) and in which group, how many days to a deadline, what "move to today" does to a task’s dates, and whether a day-start checker fires now. Measured from the TypeScript before the port.
why: Both surfaces run these every morning — the desktop checkers and dialog, the mobile checks, modal and the ahead-of-time notification scheduler — and a frontend that is not JavaScript has to run them too. The core answers ids and days, never wording; it reads no clock, so the day (and the time for the fire gate) travels in.
writtenBy: src/components/dayStart.measure.test.ts — a one-off, run once and deleted; its cases mirror src/components/dayStartReview.test.ts, src/components/DeadlinePinChecker.test.ts and src/hooks/useCurrentDayKey.test.ts plus the rows a port needs that those never had: input order, ownership by id alone and for a list missing from the map, a project parent with a lapsed deadline AND plan falling through to carry-over, cascade decided by the subtask’s own list, a settled or overdue parent hiding nothing, the stack-walk order of descendants, a future deadline and a missing deadline under “move to today”, both clock changes and a leap day, the JavaScript-isms of the day-key parser, group fall-through when a toggle is off, and the edges of the trigger parser.

Two rows were added after the measure test was deleted, with their answers confirmed by replaying them through the same TypeScript in the contract test: a-year-below-one-hundred-is-none and a-duplicated-id-is-walked-twice.

whereItLives.note: Inside cal-core, like the other task fixtures; a crate reads its own files.

notInThisTable.reminderCount: the sum of three lengths — the shell’s
notInThisTable.isMineOrUnassigned: already the core’s (cal_core::is_mine_or_unassigned), pinned by shared/contracts/taskOwnership.json; the rows here exercise it through `currentUserByList`
notInThisTable.the day-start composition: splitting slipped rows by each list’s carry-over default, the “surfaced” count that opens the review, and the silent batch’s targets (a root plus its actionable descendants where coupling is on) exist THREE times — the desktop DayStartReviewChecker, the mobile useDayStartChecks and the mobile dayStartSchedule — plus the bulk carry in both review dialogs. Not a function today, so not measurable here; the next step of the arc.
notInThisTable.effectiveForList: the per-list override resolution exists on both surfaces (TaskCascadeProvider, taskBehaviour); a later step
notInThisTable.snooze, fired markers, tomorrowIsoKey: storage and the clock — the platform’s
notInThisTable.dayStartPreschedulesOsNotification: mobile-only delivery policy for OS notifications
notInThisTable.parseCountdownDays: the global window arrives already parsed: both surfaces parse the pref with their own copy (TaskCascadeProvider, taskBehaviour), clamping to whole days 1..30. The selector itself takes any number, so the zero and negative rows stay.
notInThisTable.the trigger read twice: host-core’s reminders::day_start_time reads the same tasks.dayStartTrigger pref with chrono (HH:MM:SS or HH:MM, else midnight); the fire gate here reads HH:MM only and fires at once on anything else. They disagree on "08:00:00" and on garbage, which is midnight there and "now" here. Not settled by the port, which keeps the fire gate’s reading: a decision of its own.

notMeasurable.parentCycles: Three walks followed parent links without a visited set, and external providers can deliver a parent cycle (see the taskCascade fixture). actionableDescendants looped forever on any cycle below its root. filterCarriedOver with coupling on looped forever when a slipped task’s ancestors cycle without reaching a slipped node. hasActionableDescendants, which every selector except carry-over asks about each candidate, looped forever when the walk below the candidate reached a cycle of settled tasks — possible only through a duplicated id, since the candidate itself is actionable and a cycle through it ends the walk early. A hang cannot be a row. The port’s walks end, and their tests for cycles are in day_start.rs (`walks`), not rows here.

measuredIn: Europe/Berlin — the clock-change rows cross real 23- and 25-hour days there

shape.today: the local wall-clock day the TypeScript ran on (noon); the core takes it as a parameter
shape.anchor: a day passed explicitly; absent = today
shape.currentUserByList: the account’s own user id per list; absent = no ownership filter; a list missing from the map = no identity
shape.cascadeLists: lists with status coupling on; absent = the option was not passed
shape.lists: selector answers are task ids in input order
shape.now: the fire gate’s local time, HH:MM
shape.wasTypeScript: a row that pins a JavaScript artifact a port may decide against; it must then change the row on purpose
shape.baseTask: the Task every case’s task entries are overrides over

overdue.name: a-deadline-strictly-before-today
overdue.note: Yesterday and earlier; today and later are not missed yet.

overdue.name: a-plan-alone-is-no-missed-commitment
overdue.note: A lapsed scheduled day is carry-over territory, not overdue.

overdue.name: settled-tasks-are-never-overdue
overdue.note: Completed and cancelled drop out; in_progress stays.

overdue.name: anchors-to-a-given-day
overdue.note: The mobile scheduler asks for a future day ahead of time.

overdue.name: a-project-parent-waits-for-its-subtasks
overdue.note: A parent with an open subtask is managed through the subtask.

overdue.name: a-parent-returns-once-its-subtasks-are-settled
overdue.note: Every subtask completed or cancelled: the parent is asked about again.

overdue.name: a-settled-subtask-still-hides-an-open-grandchild
overdue.note: The walk goes through a settled node to an open one below it.

overdue.name: a-subtask-with-its-own-lapsed-deadline-is-overdue
overdue.note: The subtask is the asked-about unit.

overdue.name: ownership-keeps-mine-and-unassigned
overdue.note: A task held only by a colleague is theirs to handle; one I share is mine.

overdue.name: no-identity-keeps-everything
overdue.note: A list without a "me" (the local store) filters nothing.

overdue.name: a-list-missing-from-the-map-has-no-identity
overdue.note: Unknown list: no identity, nothing filtered.

overdue.name: ownership-is-by-id-alone
overdue.note: The same person under another name and mail is still me.

overdue.name: input-order-is-kept
overdue.note: The answer keeps the order the tasks came in.

overdue.name: a-non-day-anchor-compares-as-text
overdue.note: The day is compared as a string, and "2026-…" sorts before "yesterday", so every deadline is overdue. Kept by the port: the core compares day keys as text too, by UTF-16 code unit, so a key that is not a day orders the same on both sides. No caller passes junk (todayIsoKey, or the scheduler formatting its own days).

carriedOver.name: a-lapsed-plan
carriedOver.note: Before today only; today, later and the backlog stay.

carriedOver.name: settled-tasks-are-never-carried
carriedOver.note: Completed and cancelled drop out; in_progress stays.

carriedOver.name: without-cascade-a-slipped-subtask-surfaces-on-its-own
carriedOver.note: No coupling option: parent and subtask are asked separately.

carriedOver.name: overdue-takes-priority
carriedOver.note: A task whose deadline also lapsed is settled in the overdue section.

carriedOver.name: a-project-parent-with-a-lapsed-deadline-and-plan-is-carried-over
carriedOver.note: The overdue selector suppresses the parent (open subtask), so it is not in the overdue set and falls through to carry-over. Pinned as measured.

carriedOver.name: ownership-drops-a-colleagues-task
carriedOver.note: Same rule as the overdue section.

carriedOver.name: cascade-hides-a-subtask-whose-parent-slipped
carriedOver.note: The user decides at the root of the slipped subtree.

carriedOver.name: cascade-keeps-a-subtask-whose-parent-did-not-slip
carriedOver.note: The parent is planned for today.

carriedOver.name: cascade-hides-a-grandchild-under-a-slipped-grandparent
carriedOver.note: The middle node need not have slipped; any slipped ancestor hides.

carriedOver.name: cascade-is-decided-by-the-subtasks-own-list
carriedOver.note: Parent in a coupled list, subtask in an uncoupled one: the subtask stays.

carriedOver.name: cascade-per-list-mixed
carriedOver.note: Coupled L1 hides its subtask; uncoupled L2 keeps it.

carriedOver.name: a-cascade-option-naming-no-list-matches-no-option
carriedOver.note: Every list uncoupled is the same as no coupling at all.

carriedOver.name: cascade-a-project-parent-with-a-lapsed-deadline-still-hides-its-subtask
carriedOver.note: A parent with an actionable subtask is never overdue (it waits for its subtasks), so with a lapsed plan it is slipped, and a slipped parent hides its slipped subtask.

carriedOver.name: cascade-an-ancestor-in-another-list-still-hides
carriedOver.note: Only the subtask’s own list is asked about coupling; the slipped ancestor may live in an uncoupled list.

carriedOver.name: cascade-a-colleagues-slipped-parent-hides-nothing
carriedOver.note: The parent is filtered out of the slipped set by ownership, so it is not there to decide at; the subtask is asked on its own.

carriedOver.name: cascade-a-missing-parent-row-is-no-ancestor
carriedOver.note: The parent is not in the list: nothing above to decide.

carriedOver.name: anchors-to-a-given-day
carriedOver.note: The overdue exclusion is anchored to the same day.

actionableDescendants.name: collects-open-and-in-progress-recursively
actionableDescendants.note: Order: both children of the root in row order, then deeper levels as the stack pops.

actionableDescendants.name: walks-through-settled-nodes-without-collecting-them
actionableDescendants.note: A completed middle node still leads to its open child.

actionableDescendants.name: the-last-child-subtree-comes-first-below-the-root
actionableDescendants.note: A stack walk: a, b at the root level, then b1, then a1.

actionableDescendants.name: a-duplicated-id-is-walked-once
actionableDescendants.note: Changed on purpose in the port. Both rows with the id under the root are collected — two accounts can share an id, and they are two tasks — but the walk below that id runs once, so the grandchild is collected once. The TypeScript pushed ids without a visited set and answered a, a, g, g: a batch would have written the grandchild twice.

hasActionableDescendants.name: an-open-grandchild-through-a-settled-child
hasActionableDescendants.note: The walk does not stop at a settled node.

movedToToday.name: moves-the-day-and-keeps-the-time
movedToToday.note: A 14:00 deadline that slipped is still a 14:00 deadline.

movedToToday.name: lifts-a-lapsed-plan-keeping-its-time
movedToToday.note: Due today and planned for yesterday describes nothing anyone can act on.

movedToToday.name: a-deadline-still-ahead-is-set-to-today-too
movedToToday.note: The callers only pass overdue tasks; the rule itself does not check. Pinned as measured.

movedToToday.name: a-lapsed-plan-without-a-deadline-gets-one
movedToToday.note: As measured: the deadline is set whether or not there was one.

deadlinePinTargets.name: a-deadline-today-not-yet-planned-today
deadlinePinTargets.note: Planned another day, the deadline wins; planned today, nothing to do (idempotent).

deadlinePinTargets.name: never-pins-a-project-parent
deadlinePinTargets.note: Its subtasks carry the day plan.

daysUntilDeadline.name: over-the-spring-clock-change
daysUntilDeadline.note: A 23-hour day is still one day (rounded).

daysUntilDeadline.name: over-the-autumn-clock-change
daysUntilDeadline.note: A 25-hour day is still one day (rounded).

daysUntilDeadline.name: an-unparseable-deadline-is-none
daysUntilDeadline.note: No NaN that passes every window check.

daysUntilDeadline.name: a-month-thirteen-is-none
daysUntilDeadline.note: JavaScript would roll it over into a plausible date; the round trip refuses.

daysUntilDeadline.name: a-year-below-one-hundred-is-none
daysUntilDeadline.note: JavaScript repairs the years 0 to 99 into 19xx; the round trip refuses them. A port reading the year as written must refuse them too.

daysUntilDeadline.name: an-unpadded-date-is-none
daysUntilDeadline.note: Changed on purpose in the port. JavaScript’s Number() read "5" and "23", so the TypeScript answered 3; the core reads YYYY-MM-DD strictly and refuses it. No producer writes it: deadlines cross serde as NaiveDate.

daysUntilDeadline.name: a-hexadecimal-year-is-none
daysUntilDeadline.note: Changed on purpose in the port. Number("0x7EA") is 2026, so the TypeScript answered 3; the core reads four ASCII digits.

untimedToday.name: planned-today-without-a-time
untimedToday.note: A timed task already shows on the timeline.

untimedToday.name: an-empty-time-counts-as-timed
untimedToday.note: The check is "not null", and an empty string is not null. Kept by the port: the core asks whether a time is present, not whether it is empty. The wire carries the time as Option<NaiveTime>, so an empty one cannot cross.

deadlineArrived.name: a-deadline-today-even-if-planned-today
deadlineArrived.note: Unlike the pin, a task already planned today is still reminded.

deadlineCountdown.name: the-window-is-cumulative
deadlineCountdown.note: Window 3: one, two and three days out; not today, not four, not past.

deadlineCountdown.name: an-override-widens-the-window
deadlineCountdown.note: Five days out: in at override 7, out at the global 3.

deadlineCountdown.name: an-override-below-one-falls-back-to-the-global
deadlineCountdown.note: Zero, negative and none all mean "use the global window".

deadlineCountdown.name: an-override-holds-with-an-invalid-global
deadlineCountdown.note: A task with its own window is reminded even when the global one is off.

reminderGroups.name: due-today-and-planned-today-counts-once-as-due
reminderGroups.note: Priority: due today over planned today over countdown.

reminderGroups.name: with-the-due-toggle-off-a-due-and-planned-task-counts-as-planned
reminderGroups.note: De-duplication is only against groups that are on.

reminderGroups.name: with-the-untimed-toggle-off-a-planned-task-with-a-countdown-counts-down
reminderGroups.note: The task falls through to the next enabled group.

shouldFireToday.name: app-start-never-fires-again
shouldFireToday.note: Once any day was recorded — even an earlier one.

shouldFireToday.name: garbage-fires-immediately
shouldFireToday.note: An unparseable trigger must never silence the day start.

shouldFireToday.name: a-trigger-with-seconds-is-garbage
shouldFireToday.note: The fire gate reads HH:MM only. host-core’s day_start_time reads the same pref with seconds allowed, so the two disagree on "08:00:00"; recorded in notInThisTable.

shouldFireToday.name: non-ascii-digits-are-garbage
shouldFireToday.note: The JavaScript digit class without the u flag is ASCII only; a port must not read Arabic-Indic digits as a time.

shouldFireToday.name: a-marker-from-another-day-never-blocks-a-clock-trigger
shouldFireToday.note: Only a marker equal to today blocks; a later one (the clock went back) does not.

shouldFireToday.name: app-start-an-empty-marker-counts-as-fired
shouldFireToday.note: Only a missing marker fires app-start.
